newsitem.title: FINLAND: Tight EMU criteria key to ECB credibility - Finland.
newsitem.headline: Tight EMU criteria key to ECB credibility - Finland.

text.p: The convergence criteria for economic and monetary union (EMU) should be strictly fulfilled to ensure the credibility of the future European Central Bank (ECB), a senior Bank of Finland official said on Thursday.

"The convergence criteria should be met in a strict manner -- if not it will arouse mistrust in the markets towards the ECB and the euro," Pentti Pikkarainen, head of the Bank of Finland's monetary policy department, told a news conference.
A loose intepretation of the criteria could indicate, in the eyes of investors, that the ECB will adopt a lax attitude on future targets as well, he said.
Fears that the single currency bloc would not stand by its outspoken policies could send investors away from the euro, he said, noting this would lead to a weakening of the new currency.
"That in turn would create inflationary pressures and as the central bank has a set inflation target it would be forced to hike interest rates," he said.
Pikkarainen pointed out that the upside of meeting the criteria was decreased risk that countries would run excessive budget deficits and so likely be forced, under the stability pact, to pay fines.
"Paying fines could create turmoil in national politics," he said, adding that: "The whole set-up (of EMU) would be safer if public finances were in good shape."
